clue.text: On the street is she happy sheltering in alcove?

definitions.note: a cryptic description of a homeless woman, phrased as a question

indicators.note: to shelter something is to hold it protectively within, so one word goes inside another

parts.note: a bay is a recess or alcove in a wall
glad means happy

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a woman sleeping rough in a doorway alcove is content.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description phrased as a question, so the question mark covers the whole clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A bag lady is a homeless woman who carries her possessions in bags and lives on the streets.

clue.text: African gets rid of husband, as he works on holiday

indicators.note: getting rid of something means it is taken away, so letters are dropped

parts.note: a member of the San people of southern Africa
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: An African man leaves his husband because he keeps working through the holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the H out of BUSHMAN. A busman's holiday is a break spent doing much the same as one's usual job.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'busman's holiday' pictures a bus driver spending leisure time riding buses, so he is still at work.

clue.text: They prepare good lodgings

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
rented rooms are lodgings

explanation.surface: A description of landladies who get decent accommodation ready.
explanation.definitionFit: To groom is to prepare or train someone, or to make an animal or person tidy, so 'grooms' is the verb form.

clue.text: Tools of historical revisionists

parts.note: surface reading: implements a historian might use in rewriting the record
setter's reading: those who doctor old photographs to erase people, as Soviet censors did, using a paint sprayer

explanation.surface: A list of what people who rewrite history rely on.
explanation.walkthrough: Stalin's censors famously painted purged officials out of photographs; to remove something from the record is figuratively to do the same.
explanation.definitionFit: These spray-painting devices retouch photographs, literally erasing figures, which is exactly how revisionists altered images of the past.

clue.text: Poet makes NATO reverse negative environment

indicators.note: undoing the negative strips away the two letters of a no from the word in front
an environment surrounds whatever lives in it, so one piece wraps round another

parts.note: the opposite of a negative answer is an affirmative one
the alliance's name with its outer N and O, which spell no, removed

explanation.surface: A poet compels the military alliance to overturn a veto in its surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: A loose quiptic device: 'reverse negative' does double duty, giving the affirmative and also lifting the two letters of no off the alliance's name.
explanation.definitionFit: W. B. Yeats was an Irish poet and Nobel laureate, author of 'The Second Coming'.

clue.text: Fashionable county has no time for dangerous game

parts.note: chic means stylish

indicators.note: having none of something means it is missing, so a letter goes

parts.note: Kent is a county in south-east England
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A trendy county is too busy for risky sports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dangerous game' sounds like quarry for a hunter, but it is the game of nerve played by daring drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken is a game of nerve in which two players head toward collision until one swerves.

clue.text: Hear claim being treated as material

indicators.note: something treated is processed and altered, so the letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A tribunal hears a claim being handled as relevant evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: Camel hair is a soft fabric woven from the fine hair of camels, used for coats.

clue.text: Single text that yields many philosophies

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
SMS is the short message service, i.e. a phone text

explanation.surface: One sacred book gives rise to numerous schools of thought.
explanation.definitionFit: An ism is a doctrine or ideology, so the plural covers a variety of belief systems.

clue.text: Whip supports fund for young queen

indicators.note: in a down clue whatever supports something sits underneath it, so the first piece goes below the second

parts.note: a kitty is a pooled fund of money
the cat-o'-nine-tails is a whip

explanation.surface: A party whip props up a fund for a young royal.
explanation.walkthrough: A queen is a female cat, which the surface hides behind royalty.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitty cat is a child's word for a kitten, and queen is the term for a female cat.

clue.text: Scored an ace? You must go on from this point

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in tennis an ace is a serve the opponent cannot hit back

definitions.text: You must go on from this point
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the point beyond which turning back is impossible

explanation.surface: After a winning serve, a player is told to keep going from there.
explanation.definitionFit: An unreturned serve leaves the receiver without a reply, and the 'point of no return' is the stage past which retreat is impossible.

clue.text: Track soldiers retreating after losing their leader

indicators.note: retreating troops go backwards, so the word is read from right to left
losing the leader means the front letter is dropped

parts.note: troops are soldiers

explanation.surface: Soldiers fall back along a track once their commander is lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoor is the track or trail of an animal, followed by hunters.

clue.text: Old school friend goes in wild alarm …

indicators.note: something wild is out of control, so the letters run riot into a new order
going in means entering, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: the letters rearranged
a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: An old pal arrives in a state of panic, with the sense running on into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Alma mater, Latin for 'nourishing mother', is the school or university one attended.

clue.text: … to engage in hand to hand combat!

definitions.text: to engage in hand to hand combat!

parts.note: surface reading: close fighting without weapons

parts.words: to engage in hand to hand combat!
parts.note: setter's reading: a contest where two people literally lock hands and push

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue, the panicking friend comes to fight at close quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links it to 10 across for the surface only; the answer stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: In this contest two people grip palms with elbows on a table and try to force the other's limb down.

clue.text: Can you see the beginnings of growth?

indicators.note: the beginnings are the opening letters, so only the start of each word is kept

parts.note: the initial letter of each of these four words

explanation.surface: A doctor asks whether a lump is starting to show.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyst is an abnormal sac or lump that develops in body tissue.

clue.text: Leaders are solid, surprisingly, about it

indicators.note: something that turns out surprisingly is not what was expected, so the letters come out in an unexpected order
about means around, so one piece is wrapped round another

parts.note: these letters rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: Commentary on bosses who unexpectedly stand firm on an issue.
explanation.walkthrough: A leader in British newspapers is the main opinion column, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper leader, or leading article, is the piece that states the paper's own opinion on a topic.

clue.text: They often fly together in a row

definitions.text: They often fly together in a row

parts.note: surface reading: birds or aircraft flying side by side in a line
setter's reading: a row is a quarrel, and in a fierce fight bits of the body and scalp are said to fly

explanation.surface: A description of birds that travel in formation.
explanation.walkthrough: Row here rhymes with 'cow' and means a quarrel, not a line.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom says that in a violent fight these bits of the body go flying, as fur does in a catfight.

clue.text: Home force surrounded and broken

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
F is the symbol for force in physics
ringed means encircled

explanation.surface: Domestic police encircle a house and smash in.
explanation.definitionFit: Infringed means violated, as a rule or right is broken when someone transgresses it.

clue.text: Struggle to have fun with older anagram!

indicators.note: the setter simply names the device outright, telling the solver to rearrange

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzler finds it hard to enjoy an old-fashioned anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: To flounder is to struggle clumsily, as a person floundering in water or in an argument does.

clue.text: Picture that paints a single word, perhaps

definitions.text: Picture that paints a single word, perhaps

parts.note: surface reading: echoes the saying that a picture paints a thousand words
setter's reading: a written symbol that stands for one word or idea

explanation.surface: A twist on the saying that one picture is worth a thousand words.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a character is a graphic symbol representing a concept or word rather than a sound, as in Chinese writing.

clue.text: How old school builder schedules installation of facilities

definitions.text: How old school builder schedules installation of facilities

parts.note: surface reading: an old-fashioned way of working; setter's reading also points to traditional courtesy
setter's reading: facilities are toilets, and the women's toilets are fitted before the men's

explanation.surface: A traditional builder plans the order in which washrooms go in.
explanation.walkthrough: Facilities is a euphemism for toilets, and the ladies is the British term for the women's toilet; the phrase is the courtesy of letting women go through first.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the old-fashioned courtesy of letting women go ahead, here applied to which toilets get built earliest.

clue.text: Ongoing story of dosser I allowed inside

indicators.note: inside means contained within, so the answer lies within the run of letters

parts.note: the letters running across these words

explanation.surface: A tale about a tramp being let in for shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: A dosser is British slang for a rough sleeper or idler.
explanation.definitionFit: A serial is a story told in instalments, continuing from one episode to the next.

clue.text: Finishes after all in a dreadful state

parts.note: surface reading: comes to an end eventually
setter's reading: the phrasal verb for arriving at a final situation, as one may arrive in a bad way

explanation.surface: Someone finally finishes, but in a terrible condition.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to reach a final outcome eventually, often an unplanned one, so it fits 'finishes after all'.

clue.text: Such tosh regularly uttered when things go wrong

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: Someone always talks such nonsense when trouble arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an exclamation of alarm said on realising that something has gone or is about to go badly.

clue.text: His brain teems in comic awkwardness

definitions.text: His brain teems in comic awkwardness

indicators.note: awkwardness suggests clumsy disorder, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A character whose head is full of ideas expressed through clumsy comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes Rowan Atkinson's bumbling silent TV character as well as giving the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Bean is Rowan Atkinson's near-silent comic character, famed for elaborate schemes and physical clumsiness.

clue.text: Head off constitutional attack on networks

indicators.note: taking the head off removes the first letter

parts.note: a constitutional is a walk taken for one's health

explanation.surface: Someone heads off for a walk only to be ambushed on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constitutional' looks like a legal word but is the noun for a healthy walk.
explanation.definitionFit: To troll is to post provocative messages online to upset people, an attack carried out over social networks.

clue.text: City whose fame is based on dodgy foundations

definitions.text: City whose fame is based on dodgy foundations

parts.words: fame is based on dodgy foundations
parts.note: surface reading: a place whose reputation rests on shaky claims
setter's reading: the city's famous bell tower leans because its ground subsided

explanation.surface: A sly dig at a city that owes its renown to poor groundwork.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian city's famous Leaning Tower tilts because it was built on soft, unstable soil.

clue.text: Duke misjudging occasion for bravado

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for duke
erring means making a mistake
a do is a party or social event

explanation.surface: A duke mistakes a social event as a chance to show off.
explanation.definitionFit: Derring-do is heroic, daring action, the bold courage that bravado displays.

clue.text: Area by skip is not in order

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for area
to skip something is to miss it out

explanation.surface: A district deciding to skip something is out of line.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiss means wrong or faulty, describing things that are out of their proper state.

clue.text: Smash and grab tactic for sheep rustling?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: crashing a vehicle into a shop front to loot it
second meaning, whimsical: a raid on male sheep

explanation.surface: Thieves consider how best to steal a flock.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a ram is taken literally as a male sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: This British term names a robbery where a car is driven through a shop window, and literally suggests a raid on rams.

clue.text: Stick with drink during final round

parts.note: to last is to stick it out, to endure
to lap is to drink by scooping with the tongue, as a cat does

explanation.surface: Someone takes a stick and a drink into the last round.
explanation.definitionFit: The last lap is the closing circuit of a race, the concluding round of laps.
